neighbours.label: Emphatic ' sure' (also ' certainly') right after a subject pronoun, as in 'I sure hope', 'it sure beats', 'she sure was'
fire: The weather has been awful all week, and I sure hope it clears up before the picnic on Saturday.
This hat is a lot of knitting, but I sure wish I could finish it tonight.
Going to the old market on foot is slow, but it sure beats waiting for a crowded bus.
My little sister was crying all evening, and she sure was cross when bedtime finally came.
I sure would appreciate a more detailed article on climate and how it affects the harvest.
After that long hike, we sure were hungry, and dinner tasted better than ever before.
Your garden looks wonderful this year, and the neighbours certainly noticed all the new roses.
He sure can cook, and everyone at the table asked for a second helping of the stew.
quiet: All week the weather has been awful, and honestly I hope it clears up before the picnic.
Knitting this hat takes a lot of time, and I wish I could finish it tonight.
Walking to the old market is slow, but that beats waiting for a crowded bus.
Bedtime finally came, and my little sister, who had cried all evening, was cross.
Please make sure the doors are locked before you leave the house tonight.
Hungry after that long hike, we found that dinner tasted better than ever before.
Whether the train leaves at six or seven tomorrow morning, he is not sure.
Neighbours noticed all the new roses, and your garden looks wonderful this year.
